# Phase B: finite native-neighbour support

Candidate `CAND-FREE-R4-FINITE-NEIGHBOR-SUPPORT-20261028-870C7C4C`; author `EM-FREE-870C7C4C`.

Provisional terminal classification: **DERIVED_NOT_AXIOM**, with **PRIOR_ART_ANALOGUE / standard COMPOSE** and **RESULT_ONLY** method harvest. No new axiom, general tool family, external novelty, or Foundation admission is proposed. The raw proof remains unchanged.

## Immutable discovery boundary

Phase A was frozen before comparison. Root published all eight raw packet files at Source commit `2033a243d6e393457c49d1c2660dc1c6bf2e02d8`, under `research_notes/balanced_resume_20261028/free_round4/phase_a/`, and returned actual complete file/Git-blob observations. Only after this fixed Source return did the author open the toolbox, current-source comparison, or external literature. The Phase A record is `ANCHOR_EXPOSED` because mandatory foundation files themselves contained downstream results and menus. No clean-blind or new-identity-implies-independence claim is made.

## External mechanism comparison and actual mathematical reuse

The primary paper is Andris Ambainis and Jevgenijs Vihrovs, *Size of Sets with Small Sensitivity: a Generalization of Simon's Lemma*, [arXiv:1406.0073v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.0073), 7 June 2016, section 3, Theorem 1; the [ECCC record](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2014/077/) gives the paper history. The accessed theorem states the minimum-degree cube bound and identifies its minimizers as subcubes. This is the same core counting/equality mechanism as the frozen candidate. The original ECCC download timed out; the arXiv primary PDF was then successfully opened. A mistakenly guessed arXiv ID `1406.0075` yielded an unrelated paper and is excluded from evidence. This is a selected theorem-section read, not a claim to have audited the whole paper.

The following explicit graph bridge shows actual reuse, rather than a name match. For finite nonempty native `S`, let `m_i` and `M_i` be the smallest and largest of its ith raw coordinate, and set `ell_i=M_i-m_i`. Encode coordinate `x_i` by `x_i-m_i` ones followed by `M_i-x_i` zeroes, and concatenate the six blocks. This maps the finite native bounding box injectively to a Boolean cube with `N=sum ell_i` implementation bits. For any two native Cells in this box, the Hamming distance of their codes equals `sum_i |x_i-y_i|`. Therefore the code preserves and reflects exactly the declared signed-unit native adjacency, and preserves induced degrees and cardinality.

Apply Simon's theorem to the encoded set with its actual minimum degree `d>=k`. It yields `|S|>=2^d>=2^k`. If `|S|=2^k`, then `d=k` and the image is a k-subcube. A subcube lying in the prefix-one code image cannot have two freely varying bits in one coordinate block: the free assignment with an earlier bit 0 and a later bit 1 is not a prefix-one word. Thus there is at most one free bit in each native-axis block; every free bit represents two adjacent values of that coordinate. Pulling back gives exactly the frozen candidate's unit box on k distinct native axes.

This is `REUSE_APPLIED / COMPOSE_APPLIED` of the published cube lemma and a lossless finite graph encoding. The N auxiliary Boolean bits are an external proof carrier, not N native spatial axes and not a new native world. The coding retains the full declared native set and its adjacency; it is neither a physical model nor an information-erasing observer. No stronger prior-art gap theorem is imported or pursued.

The finite `k>=7` obstruction is the elementary maximum-of-coordinate-sum argument already in the raw proof; it does not constitute a new mechanism. Accordingly, the complete raw candidate is a useful native instantiation of elementary/classical graph combinatorics, not a new axiom or tool.

## Bounded Enterprise comparison

The three-layer coverage router searched the curated registry, method inventory with addenda, and executable module metadata. The complete result is saved in `tool_coverage.json`. A relevant navigation hit was `curation.20261022.native`, inspected at `docs/research_library/20261022/native.md`.

That index records X6 sensor fibers, finite Abelian translation observers, full adjacency automorphisms, a reused closed trace, and a separator draft. Its `X6-PHASE-MIN64` is a minimum *finite Abelian observer group order* under labeled separation and S6-equivariance. Our 64 is the *number of native Cells in a finite induced subgraph* under a minimum-degree condition. Equal numerals are not equal statements. Its adjacency-automorphism entry studies global graph automorphisms, not minimum finite populations. These indexed statements do not subsume the raw theorem at their stated types.

Narrow lexical searches for minimum degree, hypercube, Simon, and internal neighbours did not establish an exact prior Enterprise duplicate. This is a bounded search limitation, not a claim of full-library absence. One first search included JSON readback containers and produced overlong lines and truncated output; it was abandoned and replaced by filename-only `.md` searches and exact indexed-file reads. No conclusion relies on that truncated output.

The external prior-art equivalence already defeats any method-novelty claim, so further catalog expansion is unnecessary. No historical branch, task execution, or formal Task core was opened or run.

## Tool resolution and executed checks

`T7_FINITE_SYMMETRY_EQUIVARIANCE` was a relevant finite part of the equality classification: the possible sets of active axes carry the declared S6 relabeling action. The existing implementation `enterprise_math.finite_symmetry.orbit_partition` was actually executed on all 64 subsets of the six axis labels, with all 720 distinct permutations supplied. It internally verified the complete finite permutation action. The seven orbit sizes, by active-axis count, are `1,6,15,20,15,6,1`. Resolution: **REUSE_EXECUTED**. This is only a check of finite axis-choice equivalence; it does not establish the lower bound, select a canonical frame, or compute infinite-X6 automorphisms.

The coverage router also produced broad T1, T3, T4, T5, T11 and T12 matches. Their valuation/enumeration, circuit, quotient-capacity, precision, chain-complex and weighted-path interfaces do not provide the minimum-degree implication being claimed. They are **NOT_APPLICABLE** to this exact theorem; no matching operation was relabeled as actual use. The `signed.py` executable match concerns signed arithmetic roots/collapse, not the declared native adjacency, and is likewise **NOT_APPLICABLE**. Empty adjacency/neighbour API searches are not evidence of a general capability gap. No new general-purpose tool is proposed.

The task-local `phase_b_check.py` additionally enumerated every nonempty subset of two explicitly embedded finite native populations: nine Cells with raw coordinates `(u,v,0,0,0,0)`, `u,v in {0,1,2}` (511 subsets), and eight Cells `(u,v,w,0,0,0)`, `u,v,w in {0,1}` (255 subsets). All twelve native neighbour directions were tested. The four or three fixed coordinates are actual restrictions inside X6; they were not omitted observations. Every set satisfied the asserted bound, and every equality instance had the stated unit-box form. All 64 choices of k active axes were separately checked on a translated signed anchor. Execution completed with **PASS**.

These are finite pressure tests and actual tool evidence, not an unbounded proof or independent validation of the author's argument. They were performed after raw freeze and did not select the question. The proof itself remains the explicit finite induction in the raw packet.

## Review and closure routing

The post-freeze literature bridge above is comparison work by the author and is not a repair of a gap in the frozen cut proof.

The proposed bounded disposition is to preserve the proof, comparison and checks as **RESULT_ONLY**, close this FREE round after real Source publication, RA checkpoint and PRE_FINAL, and create no parallel theorem/tool family or automatic successor. The parent user's balanced research objective remains **OPEN**; completion applies only to this finite delegation.
